title: Password Spraying
overview: Look for repeated password failures across several different accounts from a common source.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Password Spraying
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: Four distinct users with bad-password failures from one source within ten minutes warrant a password-spray hunt.
evidence: Group by source IP, count distinct usernames, and pivot to subsequent successful sign-ins.
false_positive: A shared proxy or SSO outage can make unrelated failures appear to have the same source.
tuning: Enrich by network ownership and client app. Compare against the usual mix of users behind a shared address.
response: Check successful sign-ins for the targeted users, revoke suspicious sessions, and coordinate blocking with the identity team.
prevention: Use phishing-resistant MFA, adaptive access, smart lockout and monitored legacy protocol controls.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: One IP represents a deterministic fixture. Distributed attacks require additional grouping or telemetry.

questions.prompt: What is counted for this alert?
questions.explanation: Counting unique accounts prevents repeated typos by one user from dominating.

options: A shared proxy during an SSO problem
questions.explanation: Many legitimate users can share one egress address.
